span.label: The neural basis of visual memory, including how repeated stimuli elicit reduced neural responses (repetition suppression).
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: What neural mechanisms support visual memory, and how does repeated experience with a stimulus change neuronal responses?
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Reviews evidence that neurons in visual cortex respond less to repeated than to novel stimuli (repetition suppression), the neural mechanism underlying repetition priming and implicit memory.

span.label: THREE COMMONLY OBSERVED NEURONAL EFFECTS IN MEMORY-DEMANDING TASKS ARE REPETITION SUPPRESSION, ENHANCEMENT, AND DELAY ACTIVITY - repeated experience LEADS TO BOTH SHORT- AND LONG-TERM SUPPRESSION, ENHANCEMENT WORKS IN AN OPPOSITE FASHION for OBJECTS WITH LEARNED BEHAVIORAL RELEVANCE, and delay activity holds information ON-LINE
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and they do not share an anatomy: REPETITION SUPPRESSION APPEARS TO BE AN INTRINSIC PROPERTY OF VISUAL CORTICAL AREAS SUCH AS INFERIOR TEMPORAL CORTEX, whereas ENHANCEMENT AND DELAY ACTIVITY MAY DEPEND ON FEEDBACK TO TEMPORAL CORTEX FROM PREFRONTAL CORTEX
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the proposed reason suppression happens at all: REPETITION SUPPRESSION IS A BY-PRODUCT OF SHARPENING STIMULUS REPRESENTATIONS IN THE CORTEX - and STIMULUS REPETITION LEADS TO A SMALLER POPULATIONS OF ACTIVATED CELLS
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Only three short-term mechanisms are covered; long-term plasticity and perceptual learning are left out.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Hippocampal and medial temporal lobe memory (events, maps, scenes, episodes) is explicitly outside the scope.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The direct test of whether prefrontal feedback causes the IT match-enhancement effect has not been performed.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the review declares what it excludes: THE TYPES OF MEMORIES NORMALLY ASSOCIATED WITH THE HIPPOCAMPUS AND MEDIAL TEMPORAL LOBE STRUCTURES, INCLUDING MEMORIES OF MORE COMPLEX BEHAVIORAL EVENTS, MAPS, SCENES, EPISODES, ETC., ARE NOT CONSIDERED
span.note: what this limits: reading this as an account of memory rather than of STIMULUS MEMORY
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and that the three are a selection - WE HAVE CONSIDERED ONLY THREE SHORT-TERM MEMORY MECHANISMS IN THIS BRIEF REVIEW, and THESE ARE HARDLY EXHAUSTIVE
span.note: what this limits: the coverage of the review: WE HAVE CONSIDERED ONLY THREE SHORT-TERM MEMORY MECHANISMS IN THIS BRIEF REVIEW ... THESE ARE HARDLY EXHAUSTIVE
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: half the cells show none of it - FOR ABOUT HALF THE CELLS, RESPONSES TO THE TEST ITEMS WERE APPARENTLY UNAFFECTED BY ANY MNEMONIC ASPECT OF THE TASK

span.label: THE DIRECTION EVERYONE ASSUMES, REVERSED IN THE SECOND SENTENCE: ATTENTION IS OFTEN THOUGHT OF AS A GATEWAY TO LEARNING AND MEMORY... HOWEVER, THE CONVERSE IS EQUALLY TRUE - MECHANISMS FOR LEARNING AND MEMORY PLAY A CRITICAL ROLE IN THE SELECTION PROCESS THAT DETERMINES WHICH STIMULI... ARE ATTENDED
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the conclusion states it as a derivation: ATTENTION DERIVES, AT LEAST IN PART, FROM THE IMPACT OF MEMORY MECHANISMS ON CORTICAL SENSORY MECHANISMS, WHICH ARE INTRINSICALLY COMPETITIVE IN NATURE. `Attention` names an outcome of a competition rather than a process of its own
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: MEMORY DECIDES THE WINNER: ALL OF THESE MNEMONIC EFFECTS ON NEURONAL RESPONSES BIAS THE COMPETITIVE INTERACTIONS THAT TAKE PLACE BETWEEN STIMULUS REPRESENTATIONS IN THE CORTEX WHEN THERE IS MORE THAN ONE STIMULUS IN THE VISUAL FIELD - AS A RESULT, MEMORY WILL OFTEN DETERMINE THE WINNER OF THESE COMPETITIONS AND, THUS, WILL DETERMINE WHICH STIMULUS IS ATTENDED
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE TASK DESIGN DECIDES WHICH MECHANISM CAN BE INFERRED, STATED IN 1996: Quotation withheld Twenty-three years before Steinmetz2019 retires go/nogo for the same reason
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: TWO MECHANISMS PULLING AGAINST EACH OTHER, AND AGAINST THE ANIMAL: BECAUSE THE SUPPRESSION MECHANISM BIASED RESPONSES IN FAVOR OF THE NONTARGET STIMULUS (THE ONLY UNIQUE STIMULUS IN THE TRIAL), IT WORKED AGAINST BOTH THE ENHANCEMENT MECHANISM AND, PRESUMABLY, THE ANIMAL'S GOAL IN THE TASK
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE THREE EFFECTS DO NOT SHARE AN ANATOMY: Quotation withheld - BY CONTRAST, ENHANCEMENT AND DELAY ACTIVITY MAY DEPEND ON FEEDBACK TO TEMPORAL CORTEX FROM PREFRONTAL CORTEX AND ARE THOUGHT TO BE IMPORTANT FOR WORKING MEMORY
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: SUPPRESSION IS NOT ABOUT THE TASK AT ALL: REPETITION SUPPRESSION IS ALSO FOUND WHEN STIMULI ARE REPEATED DURING PASSIVE FIXATION AND IN MONKEYS UNDER ANESTHESIA - and in MONKEYS GIVEN SYSTEMIC SCOPOLAMINE, WHICH GREATLY IMPAIRS THEIR BEHAVIORAL PERFORMANCE IN THE DMS TASK. The effect survives the removal of the behavior it is supposed to serve
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the proposed reason recasts it as a by-product: REPETITION SUPPRESSION IS A BY-PRODUCT OF SHARPENING STIMULUS REPRESENTATIONS IN THE CORTEX
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: SEEING SOMETHING TWICE SHRINKS ITS REPRESENTATION: STIMULUS REPETITION LEADS TO A SMALLER POPULATIONS OF ACTIVATED CELLS, OR SMALLER STIMULUS REPRESENTATIONS IN THE CORTEX
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the change may not be temporary: A STUDY BY BROWN AND COLLEAGUES SUGGESTS THAT THESE EFFECTS MAY BE PERMANENT - PRESENTATION OF A SET OF STIMULI ON ONE DAY LEADS TO A REDUCED INCIDENCE OF CELLS ACTIVATED BY THOSE STIMULI ON A SUBSEQUENT DAY
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE PART THE ACCOUNT CANNOT SUPPLY IS NAMED: THERE REMAINS ONE IMPORTANT REQUIREMENT FOR SOLVING THE DMS TASK THAT IS NOT ACCOUNTED FOR BY THE PROPERTIES OF IT NEURONS DESCRIBED SO FAR IN THIS REVIEW - NAMELY, A MECHANISM FOR MAINTAINING THE MEMORY OF THE SAMPLE

span.note: status: A PARTIAL NULL, AND THE EFFECT IS ON SELECTIVITY RATHER THAN PRESENCE: `NOT ELIMINATED ... BUT IT BECAME LESS SELECTIVE`.
